addmultisigaddress.help:
addmultisigaddress nrequired ["key",...] ( "" )

Add a nrequired-to-sign transparent multisignature address to the wallet.
Each key is a transparent Ycash address or hex-encoded secp256k1 public key.

Arguments:
1. nrequired        (numeric, required) The number of required signatures out of the n keys or addresses.
2. "keysobject"   (string, required) A json array of Ycash addresses or hex-encoded public keys
     [
       "address"  (string) Ycash address or hex-encoded public key
       ...,
     ]
3. (dummy)        (string, optional) DEPRECATED. If provided, MUST be set to the empty string "".
Result:
"zcashaddress"  (string) A Ycash address associated with the keys.

Examples:

Add a multisig address from 2 addresses
> ycash-cli addmultisigaddress 2 "[\"s1YdUEzTzjYawpW8wkRjwa6tKJPYPvu3CwB\",\"s1hfWJ4ej1H3s8XCUb7YnrU68K64AsGVUHE\"]"

As json rpc call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "addmultisigaddress", "params": [2, "[\"s1YdUEzTzjYawpW8wkRjwa6tKJPYPvu3CwB\",\"s1hfWJ4ej1H3s8XCUb7YnrU68K64AsGVUHE\"]"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

createrawtransaction.help:
createrawtransaction [{"txid":"id","vout":n},...] {"address":amount,...} ( locktime ) ( expiryheight )

createrawtransaction is DEPRECATED and will be removed in a future release.


Create a transaction spending the given inputs and sending to the given addresses.
Returns hex-encoded raw transaction.
Note that the transaction's inputs are not signed, and
it is not stored in the wallet or transmitted to the network.

Arguments:
1. "transactions"        (string, required) A json array of json objects
     [
       {
         "txid":"id",    (string, required) The transaction id
         "vout":n        (numeric, required) The output number
         "sequence":n    (numeric, optional) The sequence number
       }
       ,...
     ]
2. "addresses"           (string, required) a json object with addresses as keys and amounts as values
    {
      "address": x.xxx   (numeric, required) The key is the Ycash address, the value is the YEC amount
      ,...
    }
3. locktime              (numeric, optional, default=0) Raw locktime. Non-0 value also locktime-activates inputs
4. expiryheight          (numeric, optional, default=nextblockheight+20 (pre-Blossom) or nextblockheight+40 (post-Blossom)) Expiry height of transaction (if Overwinter is active)

Result:
"transaction"            (string) hex string of the transaction

Examples
> ycash-cli createrawtransaction "[{\"txid\":\"myid\",\"vout\":0}]" "{\"address\":0.01}"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "createrawtransaction", "params": ["[{\"txid\":\"myid\",\"vout\":0}]", "{\"address\":0.01}"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

decoderawtransaction.help:
decoderawtransaction "hexstring"

Return a JSON object representing the serialized, hex-encoded transaction.

Arguments:
1. "hex"      (string, required) The transaction hex string

Result:
{
  "txid" : "id",        (string) The transaction id
  "authdigest" : "id",  (string) The transaction's auth digest. For pre-v5 txs this is ffff..ffff
  "size" : n,             (numeric) The transaction size
  "overwintered" : bool   (boolean) The Overwintered flag
  "version" : n,          (numeric) The version
  "versiongroupid": "hex"   (string, optional) The version group id (Overwintered txs)
  "locktime" : ttt,       (numeric) The lock time
  "expiryheight" : n,     (numeric, optional) Last valid block height for mining transaction (Overwintered txs)
  "vin" : [               (array of json objects)
     {
       "txid": "id",    (string) The transaction id
       "vout": n,         (numeric) The output number
       "scriptSig": {     (json object) The script
         "asm": "asm",  (string) asm
         "hex": "hex"   (string) hex
       },
       "sequence": n     (numeric) The script sequence number
     }
     ,...
  ],
  "vout" : [             (array of json objects)
     {
       "value" : x.xxx,            (numeric) The value in YEC
       "n" : n,                    (numeric) index
       "scriptPubKey" : {          (json object)
         "asm" : "asm",          (string) the asm
         "hex" : "hex",          (string) the hex
         "reqSigs" : n,            (numeric) The required sigs
         "type" : "pubkeyhash",  (string) The type, eg 'pubkeyhash'
         "addresses" : [           (json array of string)
           "s1kTb43xroRcuscGeiajocxn3PkRhZ9eRNw"   (string) Ycash address
           ,...
         ]
       }
     }
     ,...
  ],
  "vjoinsplit" : [        (array of json objects, only for version >= 2)
     {
       "vpub_old" : x.xxx,         (numeric) public input value in YEC
       "vpub_new" : x.xxx,         (numeric) public output value in YEC
       "anchor" : "hex",         (string) the anchor
       "nullifiers" : [            (json array of string)
         "hex"                     (string) input note nullifier
         ,...
       ],
       "commitments" : [           (json array of string)
         "hex"                     (string) output note commitment
         ,...
       ],
       "onetimePubKey" : "hex",  (string) the onetime public key used to encrypt the ciphertexts
       "randomSeed" : "hex",     (string) the random seed
       "macs" : [                  (json array of string)
         "hex"                     (string) input note MAC
         ,...
       ],
       "proof" : "hex",          (string) the zero-knowledge proof
       "ciphertexts" : [           (json array of string)
         "hex"                     (string) output note ciphertext
         ,...
       ]
     }
     ,...
  ],
}

Examples:
> ycash-cli decoderawtransaction "hexstring"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "decoderawtransaction", "params": ["hexstring"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

encryptwallet.help:
encryptwallet "passphrase"

Encrypts the wallet with 'passphrase'. This is for first time encryption.
After this, any calls that interact with private keys such as sending or signing 
will require the passphrase to be set prior the making these calls.
Use the walletpassphrase call for this, and then walletlock call.
If the wallet is already encrypted, use the walletpassphrasechange call.
Note that this will shutdown the server.
Wallet encryption is experimental, and this API should be used with caution.

Arguments:
1. "passphrase"    (string) The pass phrase to encrypt the wallet with. It must be at least 1 character, but should be long.

Examples:

Encrypt you wallet
> ycash-cli encryptwallet "my pass phrase"

Now set the passphrase to use the wallet, such as for signing or sending Ycash
> ycash-cli walletpassphrase "my pass phrase"

Now we can so something like sign
> ycash-cli signmessage "zcashaddress" "test message"

Now lock the wallet again by removing the passphrase
> ycash-cli walletlock 

As a JSON RPC call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "encryptwallet", "params": ["my pass phrase"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

fundrawtransaction.help:
fundrawtransaction "hexstring" includeWatching

fundrawtransaction is DEPRECATED and will be removed in a future release.


Add transparent inputs to a transaction until it has enough in value to meet its out value.
This will not modify existing inputs, and will add one change output to the outputs.
The inputs added are ordinary (ECC) coins only: a post-quantum coin is added only when the transaction already names
it; with too few ECC coins the call is refused, naming the post-quantum value (spend it with z_sendmany).
Note that inputs which were signed may need to be resigned after completion since in/outputs have been added.
The inputs added will not be signed, use signrawtransaction for that.
Note that all existing inputs must have their previous output transaction be in the wallet.
Note that all inputs selected must be of standard form and P2SH scripts must bein the wallet using importaddress or addmultisigaddress (to calculate fees).
Only pay-to-pubkey, multisig, and P2SH versions thereof are currently supported for watch-only

Arguments:
1. "hexstring"     (string, required) The hex string of the raw transaction
2. includeWatching (boolean, optional, default false) Also select inputs which are watch only

Result:
{
  "hex":       "value", (string)  The resulting raw transaction (hex-encoded string)
  "fee":       n,         (numeric) The fee added to the transaction
  "changepos": n          (numeric) The position of the added change output, or -1
}
"hex"             

Examples:

Create a transaction with no inputs
> ycash-cli createrawtransaction "[]" "{\"myaddress\":0.01}"

Add sufficient unsigned inputs to meet the output value
> ycash-cli fundrawtransaction "rawtransactionhex"

Sign the transaction
> ycash-cli signrawtransaction "fundedtransactionhex"

Send the transaction
> ycash-cli sendrawtransaction "signedtransactionhex"

getbalance.help:
getbalance ( "(dummy)" minconf includeWatchonly inZat asOfHeight )

Returns the wallet's available transparent balance. This total
currently includes transparent balances associated with unified
accounts. Prefer to use `z_getbalanceforaccount` instead.

Arguments:
1. (dummy)          (string, optional) Remains for backward compatibility. Must be excluded or set to "*" or "".
2. minconf          (numeric, optional, default=0) Only include transactions confirmed at least this many times.
3. includeWatchonly (bool, optional, default=false) Also include balance in watchonly addresses (see 'importaddress')
4. inZat            (bool, optional, default=false) Get the result amount in yoshis (as an integer).
5. asOfHeight       (numeric, optional, default=-1) Execute the query as if it
                    were run when the blockchain was at the height specified by
                    this argument. The default is to use the entire blockchain
                    that the node is aware of. -1 can be used as in other RPC
                    calls to indicate the current height (including the
                    mempool), but this does not support negative values in
                    general. A “future” height will fall back to the current
                    height. Any explicit value will cause the mempool to be
                    ignored, meaning no unconfirmed tx will be considered.
                    `minconf` must be at least 1 when `asOfHeight` is provided.

Result:
amount              (numeric) The total amount in YEC(or yoshis if inZat is true) received.

Bitcoin compatibility:
Compatible with up to three arguments.
Examples:

The total amount in the wallet
> ycash-cli getbalance *

The total amount in the wallet at least 5 blocks confirmed
> ycash-cli getbalance "*" 6

As a JSON RPC call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "getbalance", "params": ["*", 6] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

getnewaddress.help:
getnewaddress ( "type" )
getnewaddress ( "" "type" )

getnewaddress is DEPRECATED and will be removed in a future release.


Returns a new transparent Ycash address.
Payments received by this API are visible on-chain and do not otherwise
provide privacy protections; they should only be used in circumstances 
where it is necessary to interoperate with legacy Bitcoin infrastructure.

Arguments (the type may come first, getnewaddress pq, or second after the empty string, getnewaddress "" pq):
1. "type"|(dummy) (string, optional) "p2pkh", "pq" or "pqslh": the address type (see 2.), and then no second
                  argument. Or the DEPRECATED placeholder: the empty string "", which may be followed by the type.
                  Any other string is refused ("Accounts are unsupported"); the type names are lower case.
2. "type"        (string, optional, default "p2pkh") "p2pkh", or "pq": a post-quantum address
                  (sqf…/sqs… mainnet, tqf…/tqs… testnet, rqf…/rqs… regtest: f = FN-DSA-512, s = SLH-DSA; 53 characters) from the wallet's seed, FN-DSA-512 once
                  Falcon is active at the next block, SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s before (the YED holder policy, as
                  yed_getnewaddress "pq"); "pqslh": always SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s (larger spends, hash-based only).
                  Needs the vault upgrade active at the next block and an unlocked wallet.
                  A post-quantum address receives plain YEC; z_sendmany and z_mergetoaddress spend it (fee by
                  size, change back to it); sendtoaddress, sendmany and z_shieldcoinbase never do.

Result:
"zcashaddress"    (string) The new transparent Ycash address

Examples:
> ycash-cli getnewaddress 
> ycash-cli getnewaddress pq
> ycash-cli getnewaddress "" "pq"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "getnewaddress", "params": ["pq"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

getrawchangeaddress.help:
getrawchangeaddress

getrawchangeaddress is DEPRECATED and will be removed in a future release.


Returns a new transparent Ycash address for receiving change.
This is for use with raw transactions, NOT normal use. Additionally,
the resulting address does not correspond to the "change" HD derivation
path.

Result:
"address"    (string) The transparent address

Examples:
> ycash-cli getrawchangeaddress 
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "getrawchangeaddress", "params": [] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

getreceivedbyaddress.help:
getreceivedbyaddress "zcashaddress" ( minconf inZat asOfHeight )

Returns the total amount received by the given transparent Ycash address in transactions with at least minconf confirmations.

Arguments:
1. "zcashaddress"  (string, required) The Ycash address for transactions.
2. minconf         (numeric, optional, default=1) Only include transactions confirmed at least this many times.
3. inZat           (bool, optional, default=false) Get the result amount in yoshis (as an integer).
4. asOfHeight       (numeric, optional, default=-1) Execute the query as if it
                    were run when the blockchain was at the height specified by
                    this argument. The default is to use the entire blockchain
                    that the node is aware of. -1 can be used as in other RPC
                    calls to indicate the current height (including the
                    mempool), but this does not support negative values in
                    general. A “future” height will fall back to the current
                    height. Any explicit value will cause the mempool to be
                    ignored, meaning no unconfirmed tx will be considered.
                    `minconf` must be at least 1 when `asOfHeight` is provided.

Result:
amount   (numeric) The total amount in YEC(or yoshis if inZat is true) received at this address.

Bitcoin compatibility:
Compatible with up to two arguments.
Examples:

The amount from transactions with at least 1 confirmation
> ycash-cli getreceivedbyaddress "s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP"

The amount including unconfirmed transactions, zero confirmations
> ycash-cli getreceivedbyaddress "s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP" 0

The amount with at least 6 confirmations, very safe
> ycash-cli getreceivedbyaddress "s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP" 6

As a JSON RPC call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "getreceivedbyaddress", "params": ["s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP", 6] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

gettransaction.help:
gettransaction "txid" ( includeWatchonly verbose asOfHeight )

Returns detailed information about in-wallet transaction <txid>. This does not
include complete information about shielded components of the transaction; to obtain
details about shielded components of the transaction use `z_viewtransaction`.

Arguments:
1. "txid"    (string, required) The transaction id
2. includeWatchonly    (bool, optional, default=false) Whether to include watchonly addresses in balance calculation and details[]
3. verbose       (bool, optional, default=false) Whether to include a `decoded` field containing the decoded transaction (equivalent to RPC decoderawtransaction). Currently, only the default value is supported.
4. asOfHeight       (numeric, optional, default=-1) Execute the query as if it
                    were run when the blockchain was at the height specified by
                    this argument. The default is to use the entire blockchain
                    that the node is aware of. -1 can be used as in other RPC
                    calls to indicate the current height (including the
                    mempool), but this does not support negative values in
                    general. A “future” height will fall back to the current
                    height. Any explicit value will cause the mempool to be
                    ignored, meaning no unconfirmed tx will be considered.

Result:
{
  "status" : "mined|waiting|expiringsoon|expired",    (string) The transaction status, can be 'mined', 'waiting', 'expiringsoon' or 'expired'
  "version" : "x",       (string) The transaction version
  "amount" : x.xxx,        (numeric) The transaction amount in YEC
  "amountZat" : x          (numeric) The amount in yoshis
  "confirmations" : n,     (numeric) The number of confirmations
  "blockhash" : "hash",  (string) The block hash
  "blockindex" : xx,       (numeric) The block index
  "blocktime" : ttt,       (numeric) The time in seconds since epoch (1 Jan 1970 GMT)
  "txid" : "transactionid",   (string) The transaction id.
  "time" : ttt,            (numeric) The transaction time in seconds since epoch (1 Jan 1970 GMT)
  "timereceived" : ttt,    (numeric) The time received in seconds since epoch (1 Jan 1970 GMT)
  "details" : [
    {
      "address" : "zcashaddress",   (string) The Ycash address involved in the transaction
      "category" : "send|receive",    (string) The category, either 'send' or 'receive'
      "amount" : x.xxx                  (numeric) The amount in YEC
      "amountZat" : x                   (numeric) The amount in yoshis
      "vout" : n,                       (numeric) the vout value
    }
    ,...
  ],
  "vjoinsplit" : (DEPRECATED) [
    {
      "anchor" : "treestateref",          (string) Merkle root of note commitment tree
      "nullifiers" : [ string, ... ]      (string) Nullifiers of input notes
      "commitments" : [ string, ... ]     (string) Note commitments for note outputs
      "macs" : [ string, ... ]            (string) Message authentication tags
      "vpub_old" : x.xxx                  (numeric) The amount removed from the transparent value pool
      "vpub_new" : x.xxx,                 (numeric) The amount added to the transparent value pool
    }
    ,...
  ],
  "hex" : "data"         (string) Raw data for transaction
}

Bitcoin compatibility:
Compatible up to three arguments, but can only use the default value for `verbose`.
Examples:
> ycash-cli gettransaction "1075db55d416d3ca199f55b6084e2115b9345e16c5cf302fc80e9d5fbf5d48d"
> ycash-cli gettransaction "1075db55d416d3ca199f55b6084e2115b9345e16c5cf302fc80e9d5fbf5d48d" true
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "gettransaction", "params": ["1075db55d416d3ca199f55b6084e2115b9345e16c5cf302fc80e9d5fbf5d48d"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

getwalletinfo.help:
getwalletinfo ( asOfHeight )
Returns wallet state information.

Arguments:
1. asOfHeight       (numeric, optional, default=-1) Execute the query as if it
                    were run when the blockchain was at the height specified by
                    this argument. The default is to use the entire blockchain
                    that the node is aware of. -1 can be used as in other RPC
                    calls to indicate the current height (including the
                    mempool), but this does not support negative values in
                    general. A “future” height will fall back to the current
                    height. Any explicit value will cause the mempool to be
                    ignored, meaning no unconfirmed tx will be considered.

Result:
{
  "walletversion": xxxxx,     (numeric) the wallet version
  "balance": xxxxxxx,         (numeric) the total confirmed transparent balance of the wallet in YEC
  "unconfirmed_balance": xxx, (numeric, optional) the total unconfirmed transparent balance of the wallet in YEC.
                              Not included if `asOfHeight` is specified.
  "immature_balance": xxxxxx, (numeric) the total immature transparent balance of the wallet in YEC
  "shielded_balance": xxxxxxx,  (numeric) the total confirmed shielded balance of the wallet in YEC
  "shielded_unconfirmed_balance": xxx, (numeric, optional) the total unconfirmed shielded balance of the wallet in YEC.
                              Not included if `asOfHeight` is specified.
  "txcount": xxxxxxx,         (numeric) the total number of transactions in the wallet
  "keypoololdest": xxxxxx,    (numeric) the timestamp (seconds since GMT epoch) of the oldest pre-generated key in the key pool
  "keypoolsize": xxxx,        (numeric) how many new keys are pre-generated
  "unlocked_until": ttt,      (numeric) the timestamp in seconds since epoch (midnight Jan 1 1970 GMT) that the wallet is unlocked for transfers, or 0 if the wallet is locked
  "paytxfee": x.xxxx,         (numeric) the preferred transaction fee rate used for transactions created by legacy APIs, set in YEC per 1000 bytes
  "mnemonic_seedfp": "uint256", (string) the BLAKE2b-256 hash of the HD seed derived from the wallet's emergency recovery phrase
  "legacy_seedfp": "uint256",   (string, optional) if this wallet was created prior to release 4.5.2, this will contain the BLAKE2b-256
                                    hash of the legacy HD seed that was used to derive Sapling addresses prior to the 4.5.2 upgrade to mnemonic
                                    emergency recovery phrases. This field was previously named "seedfp".
  "has_external_imports": true,   (bool, optional) only present and true when the wallet contains keys imported from outside the ZIP-32
                                    derivation tree (importprivkey, z_importkey, importwallet). When set, the recovery phrase alone is NOT
                                    a complete backup. Back up wallet.dat or run z_exportwallet to capture the imported keys.
  "external_imports_warning": "...", (string, optional) human-readable warning, only present when has_external_imports is true.
}

Examples:
> ycash-cli getwalletinfo 
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "getwalletinfo", "params": [] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

importprivkey.help:
importprivkey "zcashprivkey" ( "label" rescan )

Adds a private key (as returned by dumpprivkey) to your wallet.

Arguments:
1. "zcashprivkey"   (string, required) The private key (see dumpprivkey)
2. "label"            (string, optional, default="") An optional label
3. rescan               (boolean, optional, default=true) Rescan the wallet for transactions

Note: This call can take a long time to complete if rescan is true.

Examples:

Dump a private key
> ycash-cli dumpprivkey "myaddress"

Import the private key with rescan
> ycash-cli importprivkey "mykey"

Import using a label and without rescan
> ycash-cli importprivkey "mykey" "testing" false

As a JSON-RPC call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "importprivkey", "params": ["mykey", "testing", false] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

importwallet.help:
importwallet "filename"

Imports taddr keys from a wallet dump file (see z_exportwallet).

Arguments:
1. "filename"    (string, required) The wallet file

Examples:

Dump the wallet
> ycash-cli z_exportwallet "nameofbackup"

Import the wallet
> ycash-cli importwallet "path/to/exportdir/nameofbackup"

Import using the json rpc call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "importwallet", "params": ["path/to/exportdir/nameofbackup"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

listlockunspent.help:
listlockunspent

Returns list of temporarily unspendable transparent outputs.
See the lockunspent call to lock and unlock transactions for spending.

Result:
[
  {
    "txid" : "transactionid",     (string) The transaction id locked
    "vout" : n                      (numeric) The vout value
  }
  ,...
]

Examples:

List the unspent transactions
> ycash-cli listunspent 

Lock an unspent transaction
> ycash-cli lockunspent false "[{\"txid\":\"a08e6907dbbd3d809776dbfc5d82e371b764ed838b5655e72f463568df1aadf0\",\"vout\":1}]"

List the locked transactions
> ycash-cli listlockunspent 

Unlock the transaction again
> ycash-cli lockunspent true "[{\"txid\":\"a08e6907dbbd3d809776dbfc5d82e371b764ed838b5655e72f463568df1aadf0\",\"vout\":1}]"

As a JSON RPC call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "listlockunspent", "params": [] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

listreceivedbyaddress.help:
listreceivedbyaddress ( minconf includeempty includeWatchonly addressFilter includeImmatureCoinbase asOfHeight )

List balances by transparent receiving address. This API does not provide
any information for associated with shielded addresses and should only be used
in circumstances where it is necessary to interoperate with legacy Bitcoin
infrastructure.

Arguments:
1. minconf       (numeric, optional, default=1) The minimum number of confirmations before payments are included.
2. includeempty  (numeric, optional, default=false) Whether to include addresses that haven't received any payments.
3. includeWatchonly (bool, optional, default=false) Whether to include watchonly addresses (see 'importaddress').
4. addressFilter (string, optional, default="") If present and non-empty, only return information on this address. Currently, only the default value is supported.
5. includeImmatureCoinbase (bool, optional, default=false) Include immature coinbase transactions. Currently, only the default value is supported.
6. asOfHeight       (numeric, optional, default=-1) Execute the query as if it
                    were run when the blockchain was at the height specified by
                    this argument. The default is to use the entire blockchain
                    that the node is aware of. -1 can be used as in other RPC
                    calls to indicate the current height (including the
                    mempool), but this does not support negative values in
                    general. A “future” height will fall back to the current
                    height. Any explicit value will cause the mempool to be
                    ignored, meaning no unconfirmed tx will be considered.
                    `minconf` must be at least 1 when `asOfHeight` is provided.

Result:
[
  {
    "involvesWatchonly" : true,        (bool) Only returned if imported addresses were involved in transaction
    "address" : "receivingaddress",  (string) The receiving transparent address
    "amount" : x.xxx,                  (numeric) The total amount in YEC received by the address
    "amountZat" : xxxx                 (numeric) The amount in yoshis
    "confirmations" : n                (numeric) The number of confirmations of the most recent transaction included
  }
  ,...
]

Bitcoin compatibility:
Compatible up to five arguments, but can only use the default value for `addressFilter` and `includeImmatureCoinbase`.
Examples:
> ycash-cli listreceivedbyaddress 
> ycash-cli listreceivedbyaddress 6 true
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "listreceivedbyaddress", "params": [6, true, true] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

listtransactions.help:
listtransactions ( "dummy" count from includeWatchonly asOfHeight)

Returns up to 'count' of the most recent transactions associated with legacy transparent
addresses of this wallet, skipping the first 'from' transactions.

This API does not provide any information about transactions containing shielded inputs
or outputs, and should only be used in circumstances where it is necessary to interoperate
with legacy Bitcoin infrastructure. Use z_listreceivedbyaddress to obtain information about
the wallet's shielded transactions.

Arguments:
1. (dummy)        (string, optional) If set, should be "*" for backwards compatibility.
2. count          (numeric, optional, default=10) The number of transactions to return
3. from           (numeric, optional, default=0) The number of transactions to skip
4. includeWatchonly (bool, optional, default=false) Include transactions to watchonly addresses (see 'importaddress')
5. asOfHeight       (numeric, optional, default=-1) Execute the query as if it
                    were run when the blockchain was at the height specified by
                    this argument. The default is to use the entire blockchain
                    that the node is aware of. -1 can be used as in other RPC
                    calls to indicate the current height (including the
                    mempool), but this does not support negative values in
                    general. A “future” height will fall back to the current
                    height. Any explicit value will cause the mempool to be
                    ignored, meaning no unconfirmed tx will be considered.

Result:
[
  {
    "address":"zcashaddress",    (string) The Ycash address of the transaction. Not present for 
                                                move transactions (category = move).
    "category":"send|receive",   (string) The transaction category. 'send' and 'receive' transactions are 
                                              associated with an address, transaction id and block details
    "status" : "mined|waiting|expiringsoon|expired",    (string) The transaction status, can be 'mined', 'waiting', 'expiringsoon' 
                                                                    or 'expired'. Available for 'send' and 'receive' category of transactions.
    "amount": x.xxx,          (numeric) The amount in YEC. This is negative for the 'send' category, and for the
                                         'move' category for moves outbound. It is positive for the 'receive' category,
                                         and for the 'move' category for inbound funds.
    "amountZat": x.xxx,       (numeric) The amount in yoshis. Negative and positive are the same as 'amount' field.
    "vout" : n,               (numeric) the vout value
    "fee": x.xxx,             (numeric) The amount of the fee in YEC. This is negative and only available for the 
                                         'send' category of transactions.
    "confirmations": n,       (numeric) The number of confirmations for the transaction. Available for 'send' and 
                                         'receive' category of transactions.
    "blockhash": "hashvalue", (string) The block hash containing the transaction. Available for 'send' and 'receive'
                                          category of transactions.
    "blockindex": n,          (numeric) The block index containing the transaction. Available for 'send' and 'receive'
                                          category of transactions.
    "txid": "transactionid", (string) The transaction id. Available for 'send' and 'receive' category of transactions.
    "time": xxx,              (numeric) The transaction time in seconds since epoch (midnight Jan 1 1970 GMT).
    "timereceived": xxx,      (numeric) The time received in seconds since epoch (midnight Jan 1 1970 GMT). Available 
                                          for 'send' and 'receive' category of transactions.
    "comment": "...",       (string) If a comment is associated with the transaction.
    "size": n,                (numeric) Transaction size in bytes
  }
]

Examples:

List the most recent 10 transactions in the systems
> ycash-cli listtransactions 

List transactions 100 to 120
> ycash-cli listtransactions "*" 20 100

As a JSON RPC call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "listtransactions", "params": ["*", 20, 100] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

listunspent.help:
listunspent ( minconf maxconf ["address",...] includeUnsafe queryOptions asOfHeight )

Returns array of unspent transparent transaction outputs with between minconf and
maxconf (inclusive) confirmations. Use `z_listunspent` instead to see information
related to unspent shielded notes. Results may be optionally filtered to only include
txouts paid to specified addresses.

Arguments:
1. minconf          (numeric, optional, default=1) The minimum confirmations to filter
2. maxconf          (numeric, optional, default=9999999) The maximum confirmations to filter
3. "addresses"    (string) A json array of Ycash addresses to filter
    [
      "address"   (string) Ycash address
      ,...
    ]
4. includeUnsafe    (bool, optional, default=true) Include outputs that are not safe to spend. Currently, only the default value is supported.
5. queryOptions     (object, optional, default={}) JSON with query options. Currently, only the default value is supported.
6. asOfHeight       (numeric, optional, default=-1) Execute the query as if it
                    were run when the blockchain was at the height specified by
                    this argument. The default is to use the entire blockchain
                    that the node is aware of. -1 can be used as in other RPC
                    calls to indicate the current height (including the
                    mempool), but this does not support negative values in
                    general. A “future” height will fall back to the current
                    height. Any explicit value will cause the mempool to be
                    ignored, meaning no unconfirmed tx will be considered.
                    `minconf` must be at least 1 when `asOfHeight` is provided.

Result
[                   (array of json object)
  {
    "txid" : "txid",          (string) the transaction id 
    "vout" : n,               (numeric) the vout value
    "generated" : true|false  (boolean) true if txout is a coinbase transaction output
    "address" : "address",    (string) the Ycash address
    "scriptPubKey" : "key",   (string) the script key
    "amount" : x.xxx,         (numeric) the transaction amount in YEC
    "amountZat" : xxxx        (numeric) the transaction amount in yoshis
    "confirmations" : n,      (numeric) The number of confirmations
    "redeemScript" : n        (string) The redeemScript if scriptPubKey is P2SH
    "spendable" : xxx         (bool) Whether we have the private keys to spend this output
  }
  ,...
]

Bitcoin compatibility:
Compatible up to five arguments, but can only use the default value for `includeUnsafe` and `queryOptions`.
Examples
> ycash-cli listunspent 
> ycash-cli listunspent 6 9999999 "[\"s1iZaRoYtafWspcieQxg6hhaU4DfZyAdGQf\",\"s1RSr6xec6Cc98emM4cdq45rkVekHMjRWbw\"]"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "listunspent", "params": [6, 9999999 "[\"s1iZaRoYtafWspcieQxg6hhaU4DfZyAdGQf\",\"s1RSr6xec6Cc98emM4cdq45rkVekHMjRWbw\"]"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

lockunspent.help:
lockunspent unlock [{"txid":"txid","vout":n},...]

Updates list of temporarily unspendable outputs.
Temporarily lock (unlock=false) or unlock (unlock=true) specified transparent transaction outputs.
A locked transaction output will not be chosen by automatic coin selection, when spending Ycash.
With -yellowback, an outpoint the Yellowback wallet layer holds cannot be unlocked here (yed-locked-outpoint):
spending it outside the overlay would burn its YED. Use yed_unlockcoin for that, deliberately.
Locks are stored in memory only. Nodes start with zero locked outputs, and the locked output list
is always cleared (by virtue of process exit) when a node stops or fails.
Also see the listunspent call

Arguments:
1. unlock            (boolean, required) Whether to unlock (true) or lock (false) the specified transactions
2. "transactions"  (string, required) A json array of objects. Each object the txid (string) vout (numeric)
     [           (json array of json objects)
       {
         "txid":"id",    (string) The transaction id
         "vout": n         (numeric) The output number
       }
       ,...
     ]

Result:
true|false    (boolean) Whether the command was successful or not

Examples:

List the unspent transactions
> ycash-cli listunspent 

Lock an unspent transaction
> ycash-cli lockunspent false "[{\"txid\":\"a08e6907dbbd3d809776dbfc5d82e371b764ed838b5655e72f463568df1aadf0\",\"vout\":1}]"

List the locked transactions
> ycash-cli listlockunspent 

Unlock the transaction again
> ycash-cli lockunspent true "[{\"txid\":\"a08e6907dbbd3d809776dbfc5d82e371b764ed838b5655e72f463568df1aadf0\",\"vout\":1}]"

As a JSON RPC call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "lockunspent", "params": [false, "[{\"txid\":\"a08e6907dbbd3d809776dbfc5d82e371b764ed838b5655e72f463568df1aadf0\",\"vout\":1}]"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

sendmany.help:
sendmany "" {"address":amount,...} ( minconf "comment" ["address",...] )

Send to multiple transparent recipients, using funds from the legacy transparent
value pool. Amounts are decimal numbers with at most 8 digits of precision.
Payments sent using this API are visible on-chain and do not otherwise
provide privacy protections; it should only be used in circumstances 
where it is necessary to interoperate with legacy Bitcoin infrastructure.
Prefer to use `z_sendmany` instead.

Ordinary (ECC) coins only: a post-quantum coin is spent with z_sendmany from its address, which returns the
change to it; with too few ECC coins the call is refused, naming the post-quantum value.


Arguments:
1. "dummy"               (string, required) Must be set to "" for backwards compatibility.
2. "amounts"             (string, required) A json object with addresses and amounts
    {
      "address":amount   (numeric) The Ycash address is the key, the numeric amount in YEC is the value
      ,...
    }
3. minconf                 (numeric, optional, default=1) Only use the balance confirmed at least this many times.
4. "comment"             (string, optional) A comment
5. subtractfeefromamount   (string, optional) A json array with addresses.
                           The fee will be equally deducted from the amount of each selected address.
                           Those recipients will receive less Ycash than you enter in their corresponding amount field.
                           If no addresses are specified here, the sender pays the fee.
    [
      "address"            (string) Subtract fee from this address
      ,...
    ]

Result:
"transactionid"          (string) The transaction id for the send. Only 1 transaction is created regardless of 
                                    the number of addresses.

Examples:

Send two amounts to two different addresses:
> ycash-cli sendmany "" "{\"s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP\":0.01,\"s1j145WNXgjEkVRGKiYJHbLXwUYWUWw9rCH\":0.02}"

Send two amounts to two different addresses setting the confirmation and comment:
> ycash-cli sendmany "" "{\"s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP\":0.01,\"s1j145WNXgjEkVRGKiYJHbLXwUYWUWw9rCH\":0.02}" 6 "testing"

Send two amounts to two different addresses, subtract fee from amount:
> ycash-cli sendmany "" "{\"s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP\":0.01,\"s1j145WNXgjEkVRGKiYJHbLXwUYWUWw9rCH\":0.02}" 1 "" "[\"s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP\",\"s1j145WNXgjEkVRGKiYJHbLXwUYWUWw9rCH\"]"

As a JSON RPC call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "sendmany", "params": ["", "{\"s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP\":0.01,\"s1j145WNXgjEkVRGKiYJHbLXwUYWUWw9rCH\":0.02}", 6, "testing"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

sendtoaddress.help:
sendtoaddress "zcashaddress" amount ( "comment" "comment-to" subtractfeefromamount )

Send an amount to a given transparent address. The amount is interpreted as a real number
and is rounded to the nearest 0.00000001. This API will only select funds from the transparent
pool, and all the details of the transaction, including sender, recipient, and amount will be
permanently visible on the public chain. THIS API PROVIDES NO PRIVACY, and should only be
used when interoperability with legacy Bitcoin infrastructure is required.

Ordinary (ECC) coins only: a post-quantum coin is spent with z_sendmany from its address, which returns the
change to it; with too few ECC coins the call is refused, naming the post-quantum value.

Arguments:
1. "zcashaddress"  (string, required) The transparent Ycash address to send to.
2. "amount"      (numeric, required) The amount in YEC to send. eg 0.1
3. "comment"     (string, optional) A comment used to store what the transaction is for. 
                             This is not part of the transaction, just kept in your wallet.
4. "comment-to"  (string, optional) A comment to store the name of the person or organization 
                             to which you're sending the transaction. This is not part of the 
                             transaction, just kept in your wallet.
5. subtractfeefromamount  (boolean, optional, default=false) The fee will be deducted from the amount being sent.
                             The recipient will receive less Ycash than you enter in the amount field.

Result:
"transactionid"  (string) The transaction id.

Examples:
> ycash-cli sendtoaddress "s1kTb43xroRcuscGeiajocxn3PkRhZ9eRNw" 0.1
> ycash-cli sendtoaddress "s1kTb43xroRcuscGeiajocxn3PkRhZ9eRNw" 0.1 "donation" "seans outpost"
> ycash-cli sendtoaddress "s1kTb43xroRcuscGeiajocxn3PkRhZ9eRNw" 0.1 "" "" true
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "sendtoaddress", "params": ["s1kTb43xroRcuscGeiajocxn3PkRhZ9eRNw", 0.1, "donation", "seans outpost"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_acknowledgerestore.help:
set_acknowledgerestore

Clear the restore marker (07/F-5, review S2): the operator confirms that this wallet's sign-once history
(set_listsigned) is complete -- every set signature its member keys ever made is recorded here, because no
other host, wallet copy or backup has signed with them since the history was taken. set_signunlock /
set_signcancel then sign wherever the record allows. Imports never clear the marker. Imported keys that are
not yet a set member stay pending: a later SET_JOIN of one sets the marker again.

Result: {"restored" (false), "pendingkeys" (imported keys still watched for a SET_JOIN)}
> ycash-cli set_acknowledgerestore 
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_acknowledgerestore", "params": [] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_create.help:
set_create {params}

Create a signer set (a SET_CREATE act), funded and signed by this wallet, and broadcast it. The set id is
the transaction id; the set exists from the next block on.

Arguments:
1. params  (object, required)
   {"seats":n, "unlockthreshold":n, "cancelthreshold":n (default 1), "slashthreshold":n (default unlockthreshold),
    "open":bool (default false), "ratelimitbps":n (default 0 = none), "ratewindow":n (default 144),
    "livenesswindow":n (default 1000), "bondmin":amount (default 1), "bondlockmin":n (default 0),
    "maturity":n (default and minimum: the network's exit window, D-Q-31), "admitkey":"hex" (default: a new wallet key)}

Result: {"txid", "setid", "admitkey"}
> ycash-cli set_create '{"seats":3,"unlockthreshold":2,"cancelthreshold":1,"slashthreshold":2}'
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_create", "params": [{"seats":3,"unlockthreshold":2}] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_equivocation.help:
set_equivocation {proof}

Submit a SET_EQUIVOCATION proof (anyone may): two set signatures by one member over two different spends of
the same outpoint. The member is EJECTED and its bond frozen (plan §3.6).

Arguments:
1. proof (object, required) {"setid", "prevout": "txid:n" | {"txid","vout"}, "rolea": 1|2,
         "sighasha": "32 raw bytes hex", "siga": "65 bytes hex", "roleb", "sighashb", "sigb"}
         (set_signunlock / set_signcancel report each signature's sighash)

Result: "txid"
> ycash-cli set_equivocation '{"setid":"..","prevout":"txid:0","rolea":1,...}'
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_equivocation", "params": [{...}] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_heartbeat.help:
set_heartbeat "setid" ( "memberkey" )

Broadcast a SET_HEARTBEAT for a current member key of this wallet (default: the first one), which sets its
lastAct to the height it confirms at (the set's liveness, plan §3.7, U-19).

Result: {"txid", "memberkey"}
> ycash-cli set_heartbeat "setid"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_heartbeat", "params": ["setid"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_importsigned.help:
set_importsigned [{"setid", "prevout", "role", "sighash"}, ...]

Import set sign-once records (07/F-5), as set_listsigned printed them on the wallet that signed. A record that
differs from one this wallet holds for the same (setid, prevout) refuses the whole import: two signing histories
for one key are never merged silently. Identical records are skipped. The import does NOT clear the restore
marker (the history may be stale): set_acknowledgerestore does, once the operator has checked it is complete.

Result: {"imported", "present"}
> ycash-cli set_importsigned '[{"setid":"..","prevout":"txid:0","role":1,"sighash":".."}]'
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_importsigned", "params": [[{"setid":"..","prevout":"txid:0","role":1,"sighash":".."}]] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_join.help:
set_join "setid" bondamount bondlocktime ( "memberkey" )

Join a set with a bond P2SH(<bondlocktime> CLTV DROP <memberkey> CHECKSIG) of bondamount. The member's
signature is added by this wallet, and the admission signatures it can add (the admit key, or current
members' keys once the set has slashthreshold of them). If that completes the act it is broadcast;
otherwise the hex is returned for set_signact on the other signers' nodes and set_sendact here. The unbroadcast
build is remembered; set_sendact on this node signs only the coins it chose for those outputs.

Arguments:
1. "setid"      (string, required)
2. bondamount   (numeric, required) at least the set's bondmin
3. bondlocktime (numeric, required) a height >= next height + bondlockmin
4. "memberkey"  (string, optional) a wallet public key (default: a new one)

Result: {"txid" (when broadcast), "hex", "complete", "signatures", "required", "memberkey", "bondoutpoint"}
> ycash-cli set_join "setid" 1 500
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_join", "params": ["setid", 1, 500] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_leave.help:
set_leave "setid" ( "memberkey" )

Leave a set (owner 2026-10-11, the bond exit delay): broadcast the SET_REMOVE of an ACTIVE member key of this
wallet (default: the first one), signed by that key alone, without burn. The member is REMOVED from the block it
confirms in, and its bond becomes spendable the set's maturity later (bad-vault-bond-locked before).

Result: {"txid", "memberkey", "exitheight" (the next block), "bondspendableat"}
> ycash-cli set_leave "setid"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_leave", "params": ["setid"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_listsigned.help:
set_listsigned

The wallet's set sign-once records (07/F-5): for every (setid, prevout) its member keys signed a spend of, the
role (1 unlock, 2 cancel) and the sighash signed. Back them up with wallet.dat (the seed does not carry them);
import them on a restored wallet with set_importsigned, then set_acknowledgerestore. dumpwallet / z_exportwallet
write them
as vaultsetsig= lines, and "restored" says whether set_signunlock / set_signcancel refuse (set-sign-restored).

Result: {"restored", "records": [{"setid", "prevout", "role", "sighash"}]}
> ycash-cli set_listsigned 
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_listsigned", "params": [] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_sendact.help:
set_sendact "hex" ( {"dryrun":bool, "allowinputs":["txid:n",...], "allowoutflow":n} )

Sign this wallet's inputs of an act transaction this wallet built (set_buildact, or set_join when it
returned a hex) and broadcast it. Only coins that build chose are signed, and only for its outputs (act
signatures added later still match). Any other spendable coin of this wallet is refused
(vault-send-foreign-input) unless allowinputs names it, and nothing is signed. The wallet's net outflow
above the fee cap is refused (vault-send-outflow) unless allowoutflow is at least that outflow. A
SET_JOIN bond counts as this wallet's when it holds the member key. dryrun returns a preview and does
not sign or broadcast.

Result (dryrun false or omitted): "txid"
Result (dryrun true): {"template":null, "act", "sign", "foreign", "outputs", "fee", "outflow", "wouldrefuse"}
> ycash-cli set_sendact "hex"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_sendact", "params": ["hex"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_signact.help:
set_signact "hex" ( "setid" )

Add this wallet's act signatures to an act transaction: the member's own signature (join, heartbeat), the
admit key or current-member co-signatures (join), or current-member signatures (remove, winddown), up to the
number the act needs at the next block. The transaction's inputs must not be signed yet (the act output is
rewritten; set_sendact signs them).

Arguments:
1. "hex"    (string, required) the act transaction
2. "setid"  (string, optional) checked against the act's set

Result: {"hex", "type", "complete", "signatures", "required"}
> ycash-cli set_signact "hex"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_signact", "params": ["hex"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_signcancel.help:
set_signcancel "hex" ( {"acknowledgerestore": true} )

Add this wallet's current-member cancel signatures (OP_CHECKSETSIG role 2 of the intent's cancelsetid) to an
intent CANCEL spend, up to the cancel set's cancelthreshold. Sign once, acknowledgerestore: as set_signunlock.

Result: as set_signunlock
> ycash-cli set_signcancel "hex"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_signcancel", "params": ["hex"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

set_signunlock.help:
set_signunlock "hex" ( {"acknowledgerestore": true} )

Add this wallet's current-member unlock signatures (OP_CHECKSETSIG role 1 of the vault's setid) to a vault
UNLOCK spend, up to the set's unlockthreshold. The signatures bind the vault input and every output, not the fee
inputs (SIGHASH_ALL|ANYONECANPAY), so build first; a re-funded build (vault_refee) keeps them valid. Sign once:
the wallet records (setid, prevout) -> (role, sighash) before signing and refuses a different spend of the
prevout. A wallet restored from a seed or that imported a member key refuses (set-sign-restored) a prevout it
has no record for until set_acknowledgerestore (after importing its history with set_importsigned), or
acknowledgerestore=true states this key never signed a spend of that prevout.

Result: {"hex", "complete", "signatures", "required", "sighash", "setsigs": [{"key","sig"}]}
> ycash-cli set_signunlock "hex"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "set_signunlock", "params": ["hex"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

settxfee.help:
settxfee amount

settxfee is DEPRECATED and will be removed in a future release.
It is strongly recommended to use the default ZIP 317 fee, which is not
expressible using settxfee.

Set the preferred transaction fee rate per 1000 bytes. This is only used by legacy transaction creation APIs (sendtoaddress, sendmany, and fundrawtransaction). Overwrites the paytxfee parameter.

Arguments:
1. amount         (numeric, required) The transaction fee rate in YEC per 1000 bytes rounded to the nearest 0.00000001

Result
true|false        (boolean) Returns true if successful

Examples:
> ycash-cli settxfee 0.00001
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "settxfee", "params": [0.00001] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

signmessage.help:
signmessage "t-addr" "message"

Sign a message with the private key of a t-addr

Arguments:
1. "t-addr"  (string, required) The transparent address to use to look up the private key.
   that will be used to sign the message.
2. "message" (string, required) The message to create a signature of.

Result:
"signature"  (string) The signature of the message encoded in base 64

Examples:

Unlock the wallet for 30 seconds
> ycash-cli walletpassphrase "mypassphrase" 30

Create the signature
> ycash-cli signmessage "s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP" "my message"

Verify the signature
> ycash-cli verifymessage "s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP" "signature" "my message"

As json rpc
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "signmessage", "params": ["s1bHiHvZu5x8yprHJbAYZtEYgfHKCdUTmkP", "my message"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

signrawtransaction.help:
signrawtransaction "hexstring" ( [{"txid":"id","vout":n,"scriptPubKey":"hex","redeemScript":"hex"},...] ["privatekey1",...] sighashtype )

signrawtransaction is DEPRECATED and will be removed in a future release.


Sign inputs for raw transaction (serialized, hex-encoded).
The second optional argument (may be null) is an array of previous transaction outputs that
this transaction depends on but may not yet be in the block chain.
The third optional argument (may be null) is an array of base58-encoded private
keys that, if given, will be the only keys used to sign the transaction.


Arguments:
1. "hexstring"     (string, required) The transaction hex string
2. "prevtxs"       (string, optional) An json array of previous dependent transaction outputs
     [               (json array of json objects, or 'null' if none provided)
       {
         "txid":"id",             (string, required) The transaction id
         "vout":n,                  (numeric, required) The output number
         "scriptPubKey": "hex",   (string, required) script key
         "redeemScript": "hex",   (string, required for P2SH) redeem script
         "amount": value            (numeric, required) The amount spent
       }
       ,...
    ]
3. "privatekeys"     (string, optional) A json array of base58-encoded private keys for signing
    [                  (json array of strings, or 'null' if none provided)
      "privatekey"   (string) private key in base58-encoding
      ,...
    ]
4. "sighashtype"     (string, optional, default=ALL) The signature hash type. Must be one of
       "ALL"
       "NONE"
       "SINGLE"
       "ALL|ANYONECANPAY"
       "NONE|ANYONECANPAY"
       "SINGLE|ANYONECANPAY"
5.  "branchid"       (string, optional) The hex representation of the consensus branch id to sign with. This can be used to force signing with consensus rules that are ahead of the node's current height.

Result:
{
  "hex" : "value",           (string) The hex-encoded raw transaction with signature(s)
  "complete" : true|false,   (boolean) If the transaction has a complete set of signatures
  "errors" : [                 (json array of objects) Script verification errors (if there are any)
    {
      "txid" : "hash",           (string) The hash of the referenced, previous transaction
      "vout" : n,                (numeric) The index of the output to spent and used as input
      "scriptSig" : "hex",       (string) The hex-encoded signature script
      "sequence" : n,            (numeric) Script sequence number
      "error" : "text"           (string) Verification or signing error related to the input
    }
    ,...
  ]
}

Examples:
> ycash-cli signrawtransaction "myhex"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "signrawtransaction", "params": ["myhex"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

vault_app.help:
vault_app "outpoint" ( [{"address"|"script": .., "amount": x}, ...] )

Build the APP spend (selector 4, nLockTime = appheight) of a vault for a module: the intents and re-lock as
vault_buildunlock, fee from this wallet, unsigned. A registered module adds its own outputs / rules; with no
module for the tag the primitive alone governs it (S-2, S-3). The build is remembered; vault_send on this
node signs only the coins it chose for these outputs.

Result: {"hex", "intents"}
> ycash-cli vault_app "txid:0" '[{"address":"..","amount":1}]'
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "vault_app", "params": ["txid:0", []] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

vault_buildcancel.help:
vault_buildcancel "intentoutpoint" ( rebuild )

Build the CANCEL spend of an intent before it matures: its value back into the vault it was unlocked from
(I-2), fee from this wallet (unsigned; never from the intent's value). Collect the cancel set's signatures with
set_signcancel, then vault_send.
An intent still in the mempool can be cancelled too: the cancel spends it as a mempool child. Called again for
the same intent it returns the same transaction (remembered in the wallet, across restarts); if its fee inputs
were spent meanwhile it is re-funded (vault_refee) with the same sighash (members sign once: a second, different
cancel signature is an equivocation). rebuild=true discards the remembered build (only before anyone signed it).
A YED claim intent (tag YED) is refused: its cancel must also refund the claim's burn (CAN-1), which
yed_buildcancel builds.

Result: {"hex", "required", "cancelsetid", "deadline" (the last height a cancel can confirm at; for an
unconfirmed intent, if the intent confirms in the next block), "intentconfirmed", "sighash", "build" ("new",
"reused" or "refunded")}
> ycash-cli vault_buildcancel "txid:0"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "vault_buildcancel", "params": ["txid:0"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

vault_buildunlock.help:
vault_buildunlock "outpoint" [{"address"|"script": .., "amount": x}, ...] ( rebuild )

Build the UNLOCK spend of a vault: one intent I per recipient (released to it after the vault's delay), the
remainder re-locked in a byte-identical vault, the fee from this wallet's inputs (unsigned; never from the
vault's value). Collect the set's unlock signatures with set_signunlock on the members' nodes, then vault_send.
Call once: the build is remembered in the wallet (across restarts) and returned byte-identical when called again
with the same recipients; if its fee inputs were spent meanwhile it is re-funded (vault_refee), keeping its
sighash. Other recipients are refused while a build exists: members sign once (a second, different unlock
signature is an equivocation). rebuild=true discards the remembered build (only before anyone signed it).

Result: {"hex", "intents": [{"vout", "amount", "recipient", "recipienthash"}], "required", "sighash",
"build" ("new", "reused" or "refunded")}
> ycash-cli vault_buildunlock "txid:0" '[{"address":"..","amount":1}]'
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "vault_buildunlock", "params": ["txid:0", [{"address":"..","amount":1}]] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

vault_getnewowner.help:
vault_getnewowner ( scheme )

A new post-quantum vault owner key of this wallet (quantum plan §4.6; quantum spec ruling C-4), derived from
the wallet's HD seed. Pass it as vault_lock's owner (or lock without one: vault_lock draws one itself).

Arguments:
1. scheme (numeric, optional, default 1) 1 = SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s; 2 = FN-DSA-512, only once Falcon is active

Result: {"scheme": n, "keyhash": "64 hex (the bytes V pushes)", "owner": pqkeyid (66 hex, scheme || keyhash),
         "address": "the PQ Yellowback address (53 characters)"}
> ycash-cli vault_getnewowner 
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "vault_getnewowner", "params": [] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

vault_ownerspend.help:
vault_ownerspend "outpoint" "address"

Spend a vault (or intent) with this wallet's owner key to address, less the fee: selector 2 (the OWNER branch,
nLockTime = ownerheight) once the next block is past ownerheight, else selector 3 (OWNER-RELEASED) when the set
is released (dormant or wound down, plan §3.7). An intent has only selector 3.

Result: {"txid", "selector"}
> ycash-cli vault_ownerspend "txid:0" "address"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "vault_ownerspend", "params": ["txid:0", "address"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

vault_refee.help:
vault_refee "hex"

Re-fund a vault UNLOCK or CANCEL spend (01/V-2): every input but the vault/intent input is replaced by this
wallet's coins; the template input (with any set signatures already on it) and every output stay as they are,
so the signatures stay valid: they are over SIGHASH_ALL|ANYONECANPAY, which binds the template input and the
outputs, not the fee inputs. Anyone may re-fund. Use it when a fee input of a signed spend was spent elsewhere.
The outputs, the builder's change included, are bound, so there can be no new change output: the new input is one
coin worth exactly what the outputs need beyond the template coin plus the fee (an existing coin within 1,000
zatoshi of it, else a self-send of exactly that amount, broadcast now, that the spend chains on). The fee never
comes from the vault's value (S-2, I-1, I-2). The new input is unsigned and locked: vault_send on this node signs it.

Result: {"hex", "sighash" (unchanged), "fee", "replaced": ["txid:n", ...]}
> ycash-cli vault_refee "hex"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "vault_refee", "params": ["hex"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

vault_release.help:
vault_release "intentoutpoint" ( "address"|"script" )

Release a matured intent to its recipient (RELEASE, selector 1, nSequence = delay; U-15: anyone may). The
intent commits only SHA256 of the recipient script, so the recipient is the argument, or a script this node
built the intent for, or a P2PKH / P2SH script of this wallet, or the TX_PQPKH script of a post-quantum key
this wallet holds (the owner's residual, quantum spec F-3). An address may be sqf…/sqs…, tqf…/tqs… or rqf…/rqs…; a pqkeyid is refused
(pass the address or the script). Fee from this wallet.

Result: "txid"
> ycash-cli vault_release "txid:0"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "vault_release", "params": ["txid:0", "address"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

vault_send.help:
vault_send "hex" ( {"dryrun":bool, "allowinputs":["txid:n",...], "allowoutflow":n} )

Sign this wallet's (fee) inputs of a vault spend built by vault_buildunlock / vault_buildcancel /
yed_buildcancel / vault_app / vault_refee, keeping the template input's scriptSig, and broadcast it.
Signs only coins this wallet's remembered build chose for these exact outputs. Any other spendable coin of
this wallet is refused (vault-send-foreign-input) unless allowinputs names it, and nothing is signed. The
wallet's net outflow above the fee cap is refused (vault-send-outflow) unless allowoutflow is at least
that outflow. dryrun returns a preview and does not sign or broadcast.

Result (dryrun false or omitted): "txid"
Result (dryrun true): {"template", "act", "sign", "foreign", "outputs", "fee", "outflow", "wouldrefuse"}
> ycash-cli vault_send "hex"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "vault_send", "params": ["hex"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

walletlock.help:
walletlock

Removes the wallet encryption key from memory, locking the wallet.
After calling this method, you will need to call walletpassphrase again
before being able to call any methods which require the wallet to be unlocked.

Examples:

Set the passphrase for 2 minutes to perform a transaction
> ycash-cli walletpassphrase "my pass phrase" 120

Perform a send (requires passphrase set)
> ycash-cli sendtoaddress "s1kTb43xroRcuscGeiajocxn3PkRhZ9eRNw" 1.0

Clear the passphrase since we are done before 2 minutes is up
> ycash-cli walletlock 

As json rpc call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "walletlock", "params": [] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

walletpassphrase.help:
walletpassphrase "passphrase" timeout

Stores the wallet decryption key in memory for 'timeout' seconds.
If the wallet is locked, this API must be invoked prior to performing operations
that require the availability of private keys, such as sending Ycash.
zcashd wallet encryption is experimental, and should be used with caution.

Arguments:
1. "passphrase"     (string, required) The wallet passphrase
2. timeout            (numeric, required) The time to keep the decryption key in seconds.

Notes:
Issuing the walletpassphrase command while the wallet is already unlocked will set a new unlock
time that overrides the old one.

Examples:

unlock the wallet for 60 seconds
> ycash-cli walletpassphrase "my pass phrase" 60

Lock the wallet again (before 60 seconds)
> ycash-cli walletlock 

As json rpc call
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "walletpassphrase", "params": ["my pass phrase", 60] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

yed_buildcancel.help:
yed_buildcancel "intentoutpoint" ( ["cosig",...] )

Build the attestor CANCEL of a YED claimant intent before it matures (U-23, CAN-1): vault_buildcancel's
transaction -- the claimed vault re-created at vout[0] -- with the refund of the claim's burn at vout[1], a token
carrier paying the holder the burned YED came from (yed_getvault.refundHolder), then this wallet's fee inputs and
change (unsigned). Collect the attestor set's signature with set_signcancel, then vault_send. A cancel without
the refund is invalid (intent-cancel-no-refund), which is why vault_buildcancel refuses a YED intent. A claim
still in the mempool can be cancelled too once all its inputs are confirmed (the holder and the burn are read from
them; refused while one is unconfirmed or the index lags the tip). The whole burn goes to the holder of the
claim's lowest-index YED input. Called again for
the same intent it returns the same transaction while its fee inputs are unspent (members sign once).
CAN-2 + C4b (the cancel-limit design): the cancel must also carry at least cancelsRequired co-signatures
(yed_getvault.cancelsRequired: 1 for a vault's first cancel, one more for each cancel within CANCEL_QUIET, at most
CANCEL_SIGNERS_MAX), each a distinct current member's yed_signcancelcosign result. With fewer it is refused
(cancel-cosign-needed, naming how many). With enough, a carrier holding them is broadcast (CARRIER_VALUE) and the
cancel spends it as its last input, signed (the CANCEL_COSIGN marker is the last output, so the set signature's
SIGHASH_ALL|ANYONECANPAY digest is the same whatever co-signatures arrive: members still sign once). Collect more
than required when you can: consensus counts the distinct valid entries and ignores the rest, so spares keep the
cancel valid when a co-signer leaves before it confirms or a reorg adds an earlier cancel. An entry this RPC can
already see would not count (malformed, another intent, a repeat, not a current member, a price out of range or
claimable) is dropped and named in warnings; the call is refused only when fewer than cancelsRequired remain.

Result: vault_buildcancel's {"hex", "required", "cancelsetid", "deadline", "intentconfirmed"} plus
"refund": {"vout": 1, "script" (hex), "cents" (the claim's whole burn, re-issued to that script)},
"cancelsRequired", "cosigners" (seqs, carrier order), "carrierTxid", "warnings" (optional: the dropped entries)
> ycash-cli yed_buildcancel "txid:0"
> curl --user myusername --data-binary '{"jsonrpc": "1.0", "id":"curltest", "method": "yed_buildcancel", "params": ["txid:0"] }' -H 'content-type: text/plain;' http://127.0.0.1:8832/

yed_claim.help:
yed_claim "vaultTxid" ( "to" "bundleHex" wait minOutZat maxBurnCents )

Claim somebody's underwater vault (yed_listclaimable): the claim-path spend at or past claimHeight, burning the
vault's debt from this wallet's YED, paying the enforcement fee from the collateral and the rest to "to".
Refused unless an enforcing miner would accept it (mempool-check-failed:<verdict>). v3: the carrier step first
(selector = the vault outpoint), the attestor fee when armed, and the RED-5 residual to the vault owner when due;
claimPath is the RED-4 clause that opened the claim ("a" combined price, "b" the emergency notice).
Refused (vault-spend-pending) while a spend of the vault is already in the mempool, before the carrier step.

Arguments: as yed_redeem, then "bundleHex" and wait as yed_mint, then minOutZat (numeric, optional, default 0 =
no bound): refuse (claim-out-below-min) before anything is signed when the collateral reaching "to" (the
collateral less the enforcement fee, the attestor fee and the RED-5 residual) would be below this many zatoshi,
then maxBurnCents (numeric, optional, default 0 = no bound): refuse (claim-burn-above-max) before anything is
signed when the YED the claim burns (the vault's debt plus any sub-dollar remainder) would exceed this many cents.
Result: yed_redeem's fields plus { "carrierTxid", "pending", "refHeight", "xClaim", "aClaim", "pClaim", "pEmerg", "claimPath",
        "bundleSeqs", "attestFeeZat", "attestPayee", "residualZat" }

yed_claimnotice.help:
yed_claimnotice "vaultTxid" ( "bundleHex" wait )

Step 1 of the emergency claim (NOT-1): the carrier step (selector = the vault outpoint), then a transaction of own
YEC plus the carrier carrying the CLAIM_NOTICE payload. Anyone may post a notice; it needs YEC, no YED. Refused
with notice-standing, notice-not-underwater, bundle-insufficient, bundle-malformed.

Result: { "txid", "carrierTxid", "pending", "vault", "refHeight", "xClaim", "aClaim", "pEmerg", "bundleSeqs", "emergencyOpenAt" }

yed_estimateredeem.help:
yed_estimateredeem "vaultTxid"

Quote of yed_redeem for an own vault (IT-9): the burn, the pool fee and, before lockHeight, the early-redeem
fee a redeem confirming in the next block pays, and whether yed_redeem would go ahead now. Signs nothing,
locks nothing, commits nothing; never refuses for the vault's state (error says why a redeem would: canRedeem is
judged on spendable YED, yed_getbalance.spendableCents, and is false with vault-spend-pending while a spend of
the vault is in the mempool).

Arguments:
1. "vaultTxid"  (string, required) the mint transaction id (the vault is its output 0)

Result: { "vault", "status", "termClass", "lockHeight", "height", "early", "burnedCents",
          "collateralZat", "pMint", "protocolFeeCents", "protocolFeeZat", "feeZat", "earlyRedeemFeeBps",
          "earlyRedeemFeeCents", "earlyRedeemFeeZat", "payee", "canRedeem", "error" }  (rpcversion 8: the fees in dollars at pMint)

yed_estimatesend.help:
yed_estimatesend {"yedaddress":cents,...}|cents

Dry run of yed_send / yed_sendmany (H3): the YED inputs the floor-aware selector would spend, the change it
would leave and, when the amount cannot be sent without change below the minimum output, the nearest workable
amounts below and above it. Signs nothing, locks nothing, commits nothing, and never refuses for the amount.

Arguments:
1. recipients  (object or numeric, required) {"yedaddress": cents, ...} as yed_sendmany, or just the total cents

Result: { "amountCents", "recipients", "workable", "stage", "inputs": [{"txid","vout","cents"}],
          "selectedCents", "changeCents", "spendableCents", "networkFeeZat", "error", "alternatives" }
networkFeeZat is the YEC network fee the send pays (YED cannot pay it), priced on the selected YED inputs as yed_send
prices it (a post-quantum YEC funding coin can raise it); null when the amount is not workable.

yed_getbalance.help:
yed_getbalance

Confirmed YED (from the index) and unconfirmed YED (mempool transactions that would assign YED to this wallet).
spendableCents is confirmedCents less the YED this wallet's own unconfirmed transactions already spend: what
yed_send, yed_redeem and yed_claim can use now (their change returns in unconfirmedCents).
Result: { "confirmedCents": n, "spendableCents": n, "unconfirmedCents": n, "height": n }

yed_getnewaddress.help:
yed_getnewaddress ( "type" "label" )

A fresh Yellowback (YED) address of this wallet. The default follows the holder policy
(quantum spec A-13): a P2PKH address from the keypool (added to the address book) until Falcon is active, a
post-quantum FN-DSA-512 address (53 characters) once it is.

Arguments:
1. "type" (string, optional) "p2pkh"; "pq" (a post-quantum holder key: FN-DSA-512 once Falcon is active,
   SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s before); "pqowner" (an SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s key, as vault_getnewowner); null or "" = the default
2. "label" (string, optional, default "") stored in the wallet's address book with the address (so it travels
   with wallet.dat; yed_listaddresses reports it); not for "pqowner", whose key stays out of the address book

yed_listaddresses.help:
yed_listaddresses ( includeEmpty )

This wallet's Yellowback (YED) addresses: every address that holds YED or appears in the history, with its
address-book label, the confirmed YED it holds, how many
indexed transactions moved YED to or from it and the block time of the last one. Sorted by address.

Arguments:
1. includeEmpty (boolean, optional, default false) also list the unused addresses yed_getnewaddress issued

Result: [ { "address", "label", "confirmedCents", "txCount", "lastUsed" } ]  (lastUsed: UTC seconds, null when unused)

yed_listpositions.help:
yed_listpositions ( "status" )

This wallet's vaults (owner key held): every yed_getvault field plus canRedeem (ACTIVE or VOID at or past
the owner height: from the block after the mint, IT-1; for VOID the release), canClaim (claimable and the
wallet holds the debt) and earlyRedeemFeeZat (what a redeem now adds to the pool fee before lockHeight, IT-9).
spendPending is true while a mempool transaction spends the vault (spendTxid, present only then); canRedeem and
canClaim are false while it is. canClaim reads the spendable YED (yed_getbalance.spendableCents).

yed_listtransactions.help:
yed_listtransactions ( count skip )

This wallet's Yellowback history from the index, newest first: type is mint, send, receive, burn, redeem,
claim (this wallet claimed, incl. its own vault), claimed (an own vault was claimed), claim_release / claim_cancel
(the intent of this wallet's claim released / cancelled), claim_released / claim_cancelled (the same, on an own
vault someone else claimed), sweep (an own vault swept), carrier (an own carrier its main transaction has not
completed: pending, lapsed or swept; plan A6), plus
own transactions with a payload that expired unmined ("expired": true, verdict "expired", typed by the payload:
mint, send, redeem, claim, register, notice, equivocation, revive, cancel). time is the block time (UTC seconds;
null without a block). A two-step action's rows share carrierTxid and mainTxid ("" on other rows); carrierOutcome
is pending, completed (the main transaction spent the carrier), lapsed (its window passed) or swept.

yed_listunspent.help:
yed_listunspent

YED outputs that are mine, with whether each is spent by an unconfirmed transaction and whether it is locked.

yed_lockcoins.help:
yed_lockcoins

Re-run Yellowback coin locking against the index (maintenance). Returns the outpoints locked.

yed_mint.help:
yed_mint cents lockBlocks ( "from" "bundleHex" wait maxCollateralZat )

Mint YED: locks the required YEC collateral in a vault for lockBlocks blocks (the term class follows) and creates the YED.
The collateral requirement, the enforcement fee and its payee are fixed at the reference height (index tip minus the
mint lag) and known before signing. Back up wallet.dat afterwards: the vault owner is a fresh post-quantum (SLH-DSA)
wallet key (quantum plan §4.3), the YED goes to a fresh holder key (P2PKH; a Falcon key from the Falcon height).
v3 (W7): two transactions — the carrier funding transaction first (carrierTxid; its redeem script commits to the
attestation bundle), then the MINT after one confirmation, spending the carrier as its last input. Before commit the
wallet dry-runs MINT-1..10 with the bundle and refuses naming the rule.

Arguments:
1. cents       (numeric, required) amount of YED to mint, in cents
2. lockBlocks  (numeric, required) lock length in blocks (class A, B or C by range)
3. "from"      (string, optional) fund the collateral from this address: an s1... address (its confirmed
               outputs only) or a ys1... address (its Sapling notes, spent in the same transaction; the change
               returns to it). Default: any confirmed transparent output of the wallet.
4. "bundleHex" (string, optional) the attestation bundle to commit to ("" = the node's pool)
5. wait        (boolean, optional, default true) block until the MINT is committed; false returns after the
               carrier broadcast with pending = true and the wallet finishes on the next block
6. maxCollateralZat (numeric, optional, default 0 = no bound) refuse (collateral-above-max) before anything is
               signed when the collateral vout[0] would exceed this many zatoshi; judged at preflight and again
               when the MINT is built on the confirmed carrier (then the carrier lapses and is swept)

wait=false and restarts: the pending completion lives in memory only. If the node restarts before the
carrier confirms, nobody builds the MINT: the carrier (CARRIER_VALUE plus its fee) stays outstanding in
carriers.dat until its window (REF_WINDOW blocks past refHeight) lapses and yed_sweepcarriers (also run at
startup) reclaims it. Call yed_mint again after the restart; no YED was issued and no collateral was locked.
At most half of -rpcthreads wait=true calls may wait at once (carrier-wait-busy otherwise).
